messages.content: Please explain me how to save this file. Is the grammar fine?

Please explain to me how to save this file.
Why: preposition ("explain me" -> "explain to me").
I am going to lay down for a while after lunch. Should it be lie?

I am going to lie down for a while after lunch.
Why: word choice ("lay down" -> "lie down").
My sister got married with a doctor last year. What is wrong here?

My sister got married to a doctor last year.
Why: preposition ("married with" -> "married to").
Mrs Rao teached us this poem in class six. Find the error.

Mrs Rao taught us this poem in class six.
Why: past tense ("teached" -> "taught").
Myself Ritika, and I am new in this class. Is this a good introduction?

I am Ritika, and I am new in this class.
Why: pronoun ("Myself Ritika" -> "I am Ritika").
We visited our village for the Holi, and we play with colours. Please correct.

We visited our village for Holi, and we played with colours.
Why: article ("the Holi" -> "Holi"); past tense ("play" -> "played").
The bus arrived to the village at night. Correct the preposition.

The bus arrived at the village at night.
Why: preposition ("arrived to" -> "arrived at").
Is the second part okay? When I will reach home, I will call you.

When I reach home, I will call you.
Why: future tense ("When I will reach" -> "When I reach").
The plain landed at Chennai just before noon. What is wrong?

The plane landed at Chennai just before noon.
Why: spelling ("plain" -> "plane").
He is not so tall like his brother. Please correct my comparison.

He is not as tall as his brother.
Why: comparative ("so tall like" -> "as tall as").
The wedding will be held at the next Sunday. Fix this.

The wedding will be held next Sunday.
Why: extra word ("at the next" -> "next").
we visited delhi, agra and jaipur in december. What needs capitals?

We visited Delhi, Agra and Jaipur in December.
Why: capital letter ("we" -> "We"); capital letter ("delhi, agra, jaipur" -> "Delhi, Agra, Jaipur"); capital letter ("december" -> "December").
Heavy rains caused floods in many part of the state. Check the noun.

Heavy rains caused floods in many parts of the state.
Why: plural ("many part" -> "many parts").
Thank you for the lovely gift, it was very kind off you. Please fix this note.

Thank you for the lovely gift. It was very kind of you.
Why: preposition ("kind off" -> "kind of"); punctuation ("gift, it" -> "gift. It").
My bicycle was stole outside the market yesterday. Please fix the verb.

My bicycle was stolen outside the market yesterday.
Why: verb form ("was stole" -> "was stolen").
Walking to school, a dog chased me. Does the opening phrase work?

Walking to school, I was chased by a dog.
Why: word order ("a dog chased me" -> "I was chased by a dog").
I am late, amn't I? Is "amn't I" correct?

I am late, aren't I?
Why: question form ("amn't I" -> "aren't I").
This steel tiffin box belongs for my grandfather. Which word is wrong?

This steel tiffin box belongs to my grandfather.
Why: preposition ("belongs for" -> "belongs to").
I like to listen the radio while I cook dinner. Please correct this.

I like to listen to the radio while I cook dinner.
Why: preposition ("listen the" -> "listen to the").
Lakshmi borrowed three books from the library, but she has returned only two of them. Does this sound natural?

Yes, it sounds natural.
Why: no error (perfect tense: "has returned" is correct).
